title: What Is Inflation? A Plain-Language Explanation

content: Inflation is a general rise in prices over time, which means each rupee buys a little less than before. It is usually measured as a yearly percentage change in the cost of a typical basket of goods and services.

In India, the main headline measure is the Consumer Price Index, published by the government. Central banks, including the Reserve Bank of India, use interest rates as one tool to try to keep inflation within a target range.

A small, steady amount of inflation is generally considered normal in a growing economy. Problems arise when prices rise quickly or unpredictably, because savings lose value and households find it harder to plan.
